manifest.name: Coding questions
manifest.description: Teaching questions and coding practice with syntax highlighting and automatic tests using your installed tools. Runs local code with your user permissions; not sandboxed.
instructions.execution: On submission the exact learner code is written to answer.txt in a fresh working directory, and tests.code is sent unchanged to the standard input of tests.program with tests.args. Choose arguments that read a program from stdin, such as python3 with ['-'], node with ['-'], or a shell with ['-s']; use the test code to load answer.txt, create any small driver files, compile if needed, and actually check the answer. Exit 0 only when the supplied tests pass; a nonzero exit means tests failed. Runtimes/compilers must already be installed; never install or download runtimes, compilers, or packages, or change machine configuration. Executables are resolved through the application's PATH or an explicit path. The run has a 30-second limit and captures at most 64 KiB each of stdout and stderr. Temporary files are removed afterward. Any language is permitted; highlighting depends on the bundled catalog. After submission, review the learner's exact code, separate thinking, and recorded test outcome. Tests passed/failed are observations, not proof of correctness.
instructions.teacher: When a teaching prediction or understanding check calls for writing or editing code, you may use coding_question. Specify the language, optionally supply starter code, and always supply tests:{program,args,code} and modelSolution. Write modelSolution as Markdown with the model code in a fenced code block and an optional explanation; author it with the question, not after seeing the learner's answer. It is preserved with the question and revealed only in the answered transcript, not executed or automatically checked.
instructions.practice: When a practice problem calls for writing or editing code, use coding_problem. Supply the host's statement, mode, optional target, and committed modelSolution, plus payload:{language,starterCode?,tests:{program,args,code}}. Write modelSolution as Markdown with fenced solution code and an optional explanation; commit it when posing, not after seeing learner submissions. Never execute the model solution.
instructions.practice.after: A practice problem accepts repeated submissions. Test results are per-submission observations, not the final assessment and not an automatic conclusion. Review the code, separate thinking and test observations, and allow revisions. Only the existing conclude tool records your final assessment and closes the problem; the host then reveals the original committed modelSolution. Do not reveal it before conclusion.
question.label: Coding question
question.teach: Ask the learner to write or edit code. Supply a language, optional starter code, required tests:{program,args,code}, and a required Markdown modelSolution containing fenced solution code and an optional explanation. On submission the tests run against answer.txt using installed user tools, then you receive the full code, separate thinking, and test outcome. Tests passed/failed do not mean correct/incorrect.
problem.label: Coding problem
problem.tool: Pose a coding practice problem with required tests:{program,args,code}, a language, and optional starter code in payload. Commit the Markdown modelSolution in the host's common field. Each submission runs tests against answer.txt and returns observations, not a final assessment. Allow revisions and use the existing conclude tool to assess and close the problem.
schema.language: Language name or alias, such as python, javascript, typescript, c, cpp, or sql. Any language is permitted; unknown languages use a plain-text editor.
schema.starterCode: Optional code for the learner to edit. Omit or leave empty for a code-writing answer from scratch.
schema.modelSolution: Required model solution, authored with the question. Markdown with fenced solution code and an optional explanation. Preserved and shown only after submission; not executed or automatically tested.
schema.tests: Required test process recipe. Runs automatically after a valid submission, using installed user tools; nothing is installed or bundled.
schema.tests.program: Installed executable name on the app's PATH or an explicit executable path. No implicit shell.
schema.tests.args: Literal argument vector; include the program's stdin-reading option. No shell expansion is performed by the runner.
schema.tests.code: Complete test/driver code supplied to the program's stdin. Read the learner submission from answer.txt in the working directory. Exit 0 for tests passed; nonzero for tests failed. Handle any compilation in this code. No runtime/package installs or downloads.
solution.title: Model solution
